neighbours.label: An auxiliary (has/have/had) after a pronoun subject inside a 'how long/far/much' clause or after a fronted 'by the time'/'when' clause; the same auxiliary in a plain main clause stays quiet.
fire: The price depends on how long he has owned the boat.
It all depends on how far they have travelled.
By the time the doctor came, she had already recovered.
When the rain stopped, we had already left the field.
It varies with how much you have eaten that day.
Depending on how long she has worked here, the bonus changes.
By the time help arrived, he had walked ten miles.
The dose depends on how often it has been given.
quiet: The boat is old, and he owned it for a decade.
They travelled far along the river last year.
The doctor came and she recovered within a week.
The rain stopped and we left the field together.
You have eaten a lot of food today.
She has worked here for a long time now.
He had walked ten miles through the snow.
The dose has been given to all of the patients.

short: aux after pronoun in time/degree frame
notes: A flagged broad pole. 'how long she has' 0.92, 'how far he has' 0.82; but 'Once the snow melted, it had' was only 0.06, and 'if he is' varied from 0.02 to 0.69, so the boundary is not settled.
